headline: Proposed Constitutional Amendment Shifts Lok Sabha Seat Allocation
metaDescription: The government has introduced the 132nd Constitutional Amendment Bill, decoupling Lok Sabha seat distribution from population stabilization metrics.
aiSummaryBullets: The 132nd Constitutional Amendment Bill removes the previous requirement linking Lok Sabha seat distribution to population stabilization goals.
Earlier efforts to pass delimitation measures failed in April 2026 after failing to secure the necessary two-thirds majority in the Lok Sabha.
Political figures have expressed opposing views on the plan to expand the total number of parliamentary seats by 50 percent.
aiContextParagraph: For five decades, the distribution of Lok Sabha seats remained based on the 1971 Census to ensure that states which successfully implemented population control measures were not penalized with a reduction in representation. The government's new 132nd Constitutional Amendment Bill proposes to detach this link between population stabilization objectives and parliamentary seat allocation. This move follows a previous attempt in April 2026, where the National Democratic Alliance proposal secured 298 votes but fell short of the required two-thirds majority of 352 votes among the 528 members present. While proponents like Member of Parliament Aparajita Sarangi have defended the shift as a necessary evolution for the electoral map, critics such as P. Chidambaram have voiced concerns regarding the proposed 50 percent increase in total seats. The debate continues to center on how regional representation will be balanced if the total size of the legislature is expanded.
whyItIsViral: The story is being actively covered by three independent news outlets, reflecting significant political interest in parliamentary restructuring.
